In accordance with WAC 47563-100,-th e Appellants haves filed exceptions to the
Proposed Decisions issued on January 21, 2011, following a hearing conducted by Terry
Sebring, Chair, and presiding officer for the Board ofTax Appeals (Board).
In order for this Board to reconsider the decisions set forth in the Proposed Decisions, it
must be clear that thepresiding officer did not properly consider the evidence or that there was
an omission ofcertain pertinent facts or amisapplication ofthe law.
The Board reviewed the written exceptions, the Proposed Decisions issued, and all
available information and material. We conclude that the issues raised by the Appellants were
adequately addressed in the Proposed Decisions, and that the evidence and law were properly
considered and applied. The Board finds no basis for changing the decisions. Therefore, we
deny the exceptions and adopt the Proposed Decisions as the Final Decisions ofthis Board.

ISSUES
The issues in these appeals are the January 1, 2009, market values ofproperties located in
Thorp, Washington.
PROCEDURAL RULINGS
During the Board's introductory remarks, the Owner objected to the consideration ofthe
Assessors' exhibits received by the Board on December 28, 2010. The Assessor replied that the
documents were mailed in compliance with the Board rules, WAC 45506511-( 0-)whic,h
requires "documentary evidence which is to be introduced at the hearing shall be submitted to
theboard together with proofofservice pursuant to WAC 445161- 00-at least 10 business days
prior to hearing."A lso, see RCW 8202002..30.The Owner states she received the Assessor's
materials, but they were filed late and should not be considered.

The Board notes that, ifthe documentary evidence ofboth parties are not considered

before the Board and would fail to meet its burden ofproof, since its chose to rely on only its
documents, not new sworn testimony. Evennew sworn testimony from the Owner would not
have cured its failure to file its evidence documents in atimely fashion.
FACTS AND CONTENTIONS
The subject property is approximately 139 lots; only about 122 lots are appealed. The
lots are all vacant, with the exception offive lots, which contain improvements related to the
farming activity, or are a family members' home, see Docket Nos. 73206, 73212, 73217, and
73260 in these appeals. The Board does not describe the improvements, because the Owner does
not dispute the value ofthe improvements; she only disputes the fairmarket value ofthe land.
The vacant lots range from 3.0 to 144.8 acres. Most ofthe lots are 30. acres.
Only three ofthe larger lots have improvements located upon them.
O The zoning is AG-3. ;it allows one building siteper threea- cre or larger parcel.
The Assessor states that the farms are located 8 to 10 miles east ofEllensburg,
and south ofInterstate 90.
Both ofthe farms are irrigated land.
All ofthe land is in the open space - farm / agriculture classification. The land
with improvements is also part ofthe open space classification because each of
the farms is more than 20 acres ofadjacent land. The improvements are valued at
fairmarket value; the open.s pace valuation applies only to the land.

The following considers all ofthe documentary evidence, based upon the finding that all
were submitted by the County Board to this Board, notby the parties.
The Owner's Attorney argues viaunsworn comments that Owner's evidence states:
The Owner indicated she created the lots by the segregation process in 2005 or 2006.
The Owner submitted the segregation and had the new platted lots surveyed. The plat has
road easements on it also; none ofthe easement roads shown on theplat had been
constructed.
The Owner plats did not have to be approved bythe Kittitas County Planning Department
orits planningp, rocess, because the lots are 3.0 acres and larger in size, and the
segregations comply with the AG-3 zoning.
The Owner indicated that the plats were filed in 2005 or 2006 in order to avoid a future
change in theplanning process that might require County approval ofthe Owners'
parcels plat request.
The Owner indicated she had no immediateplans to sell the lots. None ofthe lots have
been marketed for sale. The current market for lots is nonexistent.

ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSIONS
This Boards' goal in its hearings is to hear and weigh evidence to support a determination
oftrue and fair value as defined by statute 15 and the Washington Administrative Code. 1 6 Under
the provisions ofRCW 80434.00.and WAC 40583-007,-th e trueand fair value ofproperty shall
bebased upon sales ofthe subject property or sales ofcomparable properties made within the
past five years. The Assessor is afforded considerable discretion to determine the methodology
employed to arrive at market
value.7" "
Market value"m eans the amount ofmoney a willing
18
purchaser would pay to a willing seller.
The Assessor's valuation is presumed to be correct, and can be overcome only by
presentation of c"lear, cogent and convincing" evidence that the value is erroneous." Clear,
cogent, and convincing evidence means a quantum ofproofthat is less than beyond areasonable
doubt,b utmore than amere preponderance ofthe evidence. It is the quantum ofevidence
necessaryto convince the trier offact that the ultimate fact in issue is "highly probable.2" 0
The decision ofthe County Board is entitled to no evidentiary weightbefore this Board.
This hearing is considered de novo, or new.
Both parties present multiple sales. Neitherparty presents amap showing the location of
their sales or information showing specific features ofthe sales' properties such as view,
topography, etc. Neither party provides specific comparable sales from their sales or
adjustments ofthose sales to the subject parcels. The Owner does not provide expert appraisal
testimony, in fact no sworn testimony is provided at all. The Owner's evidence documents list
some sales viaREETAs, but the size ofthe sale properties is not provided. No market analysis
or value opinion is provided in the Owner's documents. The Assessor's testimony points out
that most ofthe Owner's sales are not fair market value transactions. The Owner provides only a
general value request ofbetween $30,00 to $60,00 per acre.
The Board finds the Owner fails to meet the burden ofproof. The Assessor notes that
most ofthe Owner's sales are not fair market value sales and should not be considered. The
Board agrees. The Owner provides no sworn testimony, sales analysis, or market comparisons:
